messages:
Nate: quick RFC follow-up idea — introduce a "warmup transaction" (wtx) marker to make manifestless shard updates atomic for readers. idea: upload a wtx object that lists shard pieces + checksums + a commit state. readers only treat shards active once wtx.state == "committed". this avoids partial-hotstart races.

Sanjay: sounds promising. main worry is KV cache coherence — if readers see shards before commit we get weird mixes. how do we prevent double reads + wasted prefetch?

Nate: exactly, plan is: prefetchers can see an "announced" state and start best-effort fetch, but runtime must ignore shards until "committed". prefetch is optimistic. if commit fails, prefetch is evicted.

Mia: extra S3/registry ops though. each deploy = extra small put/read for the wtx object. cost/latency ok?

Devon: overhead small compared to full shard pushes. plus we can batch wtx for multi-shard model rollouts. concern: tail latency if verification slows commit. need a soft-fallback path.

Nate: proposal for 3-phase rollout: 1) announce (wtx.state=announced) -> prefetch allowed but not active, 2) verify (background checksum/compat checks), 3) commit (wtx.state=committed) -> activate. if verify times out -> mark wtx.failed and runtime falls back to old model.

Olivia: signing/KMS requirement: wtx should be signed (HSM) or at least KMS-signed to prevent malicious swaps in private deployments. otherwise a waiter attack could flip wtx.

Nate: agreed. wtx schema sketch: 
```json
{
  "wtxid": "wtx-2027-05-12-1234",
  "model": "ggml-demo-v1",
  "shards": [
    {"path": "s3://bucket/m/model-0000.safetensors", "sha256": "..."},
    {"path": "s3://bucket/m/model-0001.safetensors", "sha256": "..."}
  ],
  "state": "announced|verifying|committed|failed",
  "signed_by": "kms:key-abc",
  "issued_at": "1799054321"
}
```

Sanjay: runtime needs rules for prefetch eviction: if wtx.failed or ttl expired, purge caches to avoid serving partial weights. propose ttl default 1h.

Mia: how do we handle Private/OnPrem where object store semantics differ? need a feature-flagged path to skip signing or use local signer. also upgrade path for older agents.

Devon: operational signals we should emit: wtx_verify_latency, wtx_commit_rate, wtx_verify_fail_rate, wtx_active_count. these help detect regressions in commit gating.

Nate: rollout plan I propose: canary metadata-only (announce but treat as committed) -> verify+metrics (observe verify failures without gating) -> enforced gating (runtime honors committed only). feature flag + opt-in per deployment.

Olivia: HSM/KMS integration + audit logs should be mandatory for Dedicated/Private at enforcement phase. for hosted we can use internal signing.

InfraBot: deploybot: created canary rollout job wtx-canary-2027-05-12, target=eng-ml-canary, eta=10m :rocket:

Mia: ok — next steps: write up a small RFC addendum with schema + TTL defaults + three-phase rollout. I'll own the doc.

Nate: thanks — will sketch runtime changes (prefetch semantics + cache eviction) and add the metric hooks.

Devon: +1, add tests for race where verify completes after partial activation in older nodes.

Sanjay: noted. will add eviction playbook (how to roll back if a commit fails mid-rollout).

Olivia: tagging security for KMS design review.

Mia: acked. :thumbsup:
